Content:
Consider the two vectors [MATH: \mathbf{a}=\langle 1,-2, 2 \rangle] and [MATH: \mathbf{b}=\langle 3,0,-1 \rangle] shown in the picture below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/05a9116a219fa5c7e3a9cffa70876d2d]

Content:
To find the angle [MATH: \theta] between the vectors, we can rearrange the dot product formula:

Content:
[MATH: a ⋅ b|=|a|⋅|b|⋅ \cos θ; \cos θ|= (a ⋅ b)/(|a||b|); θ|= \arccos ((a ⋅ b)/(|a||b|))]

Content:
The dot product is given by

Content:
[MATH: a ⋅ b|= a_{x}b_{x} + a_{y}b_{y} + a_{z}b_{z}; = 1 ⋅ 3 + (− 2) ⋅ 0 + 2 ⋅ (− 1); = 1,]

Content:
and the magnitudes of [MATH: \mathbf{a}] and [MATH: \mathbf{b}] are

Content:
[MATH: |a||= sqrt(a_{x}^{2} + a_{y}^{2} + a_{z}^{2}); = sqrt(1^{2} + (− 2)^{2} + 2^{2}); = 3,;|b||= sqrt(b_{x}^{2} + b_{y}^{2} + b_{z}^{2}); = sqrt(3^{2} + 0^{2} + (− 1)^{2}); = sqrt(10).]

Content:
Therefore,

Content:
[MATH: \theta = \arccos \Bigg( \dfrac{1}{3\sqrt{10}} \Bigg) \approx 83.9^\circ.]
